artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d \geq 4$ and a set $P$ of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, let $D(P)$ denote the number of distinct values in the multiset $\{\,\|p-q\| : p,q \in P,\ p \neq q\,\}$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is the Euclidean norm. A hypersphere in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a set of the form $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^d : \|x - c\| = r\}$ for some center $c \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and radius $r > 0$. Define
$$D_d^{\circ}(n) \;=\; \min\bigl\{ D(P) : P \subset \mathbb{R}^d,\ |P|=n,\ P \text{ lies on some hypersphere in } \mathbb{R}^d \bigr\}.$$
It is known that $D_4^{\circ}(n) = O(n/\log\log n)$ and $D_d^{\circ}(n) = O(n^{2/(d-2)})$ for $d > 4$, and trivially $D_d^{\circ}(n) \geq D_d(n)$, where $D_d(n)$ is the minimum number of distinct distances determined by any $n$-point set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Determine the asymptotic order of $D_d^{\circ}(n)$ as $n \to \infty$, for each fixed $d \geq 4$.
artifact.status_search_result: No matching lower bounds beyond the trivial $D_d^{\circ}(n) \geq D_d(n)$ appear in the literature, and no result establishing the asymptotic order of distinct distances for points constrained to lie on a hypersphere in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d \geq 4$ was located. The problem appears to remain open.
